context: Three-panel linked dashboard: a rotatable orthographic globe (canvas) showing 500 synthetic earthquakes colored by depth via plasma scale, a scatter plot of depth vs magnitude with brush selection, and a ridgeline KDE plot showing depth distributions across 6 tectonic zones.
first_impression: Visually polished and spatially coherent — the dark theme lets the plasma depth colors read clearly across all three panels without competing for attention.
what_works: The plasma depth colorscale is immediately legible on both the globe and scatter; shallow-to-deep shifts from yellow to purple are intuitive and consistent across panels. The ridgeline chart effectively differentiates the 6 zones — each has a distinct depth profile and the KDE curves are spaced with enough overlap to compare without confusion.
what_doesnt: The zone legend is truncated to 4 of 6 zones in code (`zoneNames.slice(0, 4)`), leaving Cascadia/Alaska and Himalayan Front unlabeled in the ridgeline — a direct readability bug. The two color systems (continuous plasma for depth on globe/scatter, categorical 6-color for zones on ridgeline) cannot be cross-referenced: you cannot identify which zone a globe point belongs to, fragmenting the linked-view story.
